questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests ability to design a runtime-extensible backend with a clean interface, minimal FAB (feature-flag) API, and safe runtime swapping.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy pattern for pluggable backends
- Registry for runtime extension
- Atomic swap and cache coherence trade-offs

## Code Example

```javascript
// Interfaces and usage sketch
interface IFlagBackend { getFlag(name:string, context?:any): boolean; }
class FlagCore { constructor(private backend:IFlagBackend){ } isEnabled(name:string, ctx?:any){ return this.backend.getFlag(name, ctx); } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test swapping backends without downtime?
- How would you implement per-tenant flags and cache invalidation?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to design for runtime extensibility and reliability in a pluggable notification system.

## Key Concepts

- **Registry-driven plugins**: Channels are registered at runtime via a central registry, enabling new channel types without recompiling the core dispatcher.
- **Channel interface and factories**: A standardized contract ensures all notification channels implement common behavior while factories handle instantiation.
- **Per-user preferences**: Respect individual user settings for preferred notification channels and delivery priority.
- **Fallback strategy**: A reliable rollback mechanism ensures notifications are delivered even when primary channels fail.
